first.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not a defensive reaction to the competitor. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting response to aggressive entry pricing and would likely win SMB acquisition, but the inherited record explicitly flags materially reduced 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it — that is a downstream value risk that trades long-term qualified revenue for short-term volume, so I am declining it despite the competitive pressure. Referral incentive (memory_57) is safe but addresses neither of the two metrics actually declining. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different segment and does not touch the observed regressions. That leaves two live candidates aimed at the actual declines: simplify_onboarding (memory_31, memory_86) and activation_messaging (memory_91). I intend simplify_onboarding because it is supported by two independent records, it directly targets the onboarding completion drop, and both records connect it to activation lift as well — so it plausibly addresses the 6% activation decline and the 4% completion decline with one slot, while also improving time-to-value against a cheaper competitor without discounting. I am spending verification on the two candidates that would actually change my decision: memory_86 because it is the closest fit to the current onboarding regression and I want to confirm the lift was on completion and time-to-value rather than a vanity step-through metric, and memory_91 because activation messaging is the strongest alternative and if its effect on first meaningful action is larger or more durable than the onboarding records, I should switch. I am deliberately not spending budget on memory_73, since verifying it would not change an action I have already declined. Key uncertainties I am not resolving: these records are 24-64 days old and predate the competitor's entry, so prior lifts may not replicate under changed market conditions; the declines may be driven by a shift in inbound traffic mix (more price-shoppers, lower intent) rather than by onboarding friction, in which case a funnel fix will underperform; and memory_31 and memory_86 may not be independent evidence if they measured overlapping cohorts. I am running this at standard experiment scale with a holdout and pre-committed retention-inclusive readout rather than a broad rollout, so that a null or traffic-mix-driven result is detectable rather than assumed away.

final.rationale: Verification confirmed both candidates, and simplify_onboarding is the stronger choice. exp_86 shows completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3% — the retention sign is positive, which is exactly what the primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) requires. exp_91 is also real but smaller on the retention dimension (+1%) and narrower in scope. Shortened onboarding directly attacks the 4% completion decline, and the faster time-to-value is the honest competitive answer to a cheaper rival: win on speed to value rather than on price. I am holding the line against promotional_pricing (memory_73) even though it is the most direct response to the competitor's entry pricing — that record explicitly documents materially reduced 30-day retention and warns against generalizing it, so it would purchase acquisition volume by degrading the retention base that long-term qualified revenue depends on. referral_incentive (memory_57) is safe but touches neither declining metric; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets a different segment entirely. One correction to my prior reasoning that the archive forced: exp_86 did not actually measure an activation lift. It measured completion, time-to-value, and retention. My earlier claim that onboarding would address both declines with one slot was an overreach — the activation link is inferred from the time-to-value improvement, not demonstrated. exp_91 is the record that directly evidences activation (+6%), and I am declining it this week on retention magnitude, which means the 6% activation decline may go only partially addressed. If the readout shows completion recovering while activation stays flat, activation_messaging is the clear next slot. Remaining uncertainties I am not resolving: all these records predate the competitor's entry, so prior effect sizes may not replicate under a changed traffic mix; the declines could be driven by lower-intent price-shopping inbound rather than funnel friction, in which case a funnel fix underperforms regardless of how good exp_86 was; and memory_31 and memory_86 may share overlapping cohorts, so they are not fully independent confirmation. I am therefore running a standard experiment with a holdout and a pre-committed readout that includes 30-day retention and segment-level traffic mix, not a broad rollout — a null or mix-driven result must be detectable rather than assumed away.
